reasoning: B wins narrowly. Both attempts are correct and treat remote input as untrusted. B closes a real race: a PlaceBlock request processed after PlayerRemoving would leave an orphan block in A. A's advantage, the Destroying hook, only matters if other code destroys blocks, and no such code exists yet. A's comments are slightly better, and B's could be one line instead of two. Even so, B's behaviour is a bit more robust and its code is cleaner, and that counts for more here.

criteria.note: Creates both remotes and the PlacedBlocks folder, validates through PlacementRules.validate, builds the part from BlockTypes.STYLES, and enforces the cap and the 0.1 s cooldown; the Destroying hook keeps counts right on every removal path, but a PlaceBlock request already queued when the player leaves can still add a block that nothing will clean up.
blockType and position are typed unknown and passed to validate, and RemoveBlock checks typeof, IsA("BasePart") and the server-side ownerOf[block] == player before Destroy.
All three comments carry real reasons: ownership is kept server-side, the attribute is for the UI and not trusted, and Destroying covers external destruction; '-- seconds' gives the unit.
Each comment is one short line placed next to the code it governs, with no banners.
No change history or references to the request.
Reuses BLOCK_SIZE and STYLES, is strict-typed and passes all checks; the warn on every rejected placement could spam the server log.

Creates both remotes and the folder, uses validate and STYLES, and enforces the cap and cooldown; the player.Parent ~= Players guard stops placements that arrive after the player has left, but counts drift if a block is destroyed outside removeBlock.
Checks typeof, IsA and blockOwners[block] == player before removing, and also checks typeof(result) == "Vector3" after validation.
Its one comment explains the leave/queue race that the Parent guard prevents, which the code can't show on its own.
The race comment takes two lines where one would do.
Reuses the shared modules, has clean named handlers and a central removeBlock helper, is typed, and passes all checks.

strengths: Destroying-based tracking keeps counts correct however a block is removed
Ownership checked against a server-side table
weaknesses: A placement request queued just before the player leaves can leave an orphan block
warn on every rejection lets a client spam the server log

strengths: Guards against placements processed after the player leaves, which prevents orphan blocks
